items.title: Ep43. Whoosh! What makes wind?
items.desc: In this episode, Lily and Max follow the clues to discover what makes wind. They explore how differences in air pressure get air moving, why wind can change speed and direction, and how thunderstorms can bring sudden gusts. Plus, Max learns what a “southerly” really means and finds out that even a paper windmill can help us spot the wind!

items.title: Ep42. Why do bats hang upside down?
items.desc: In this episode, Lily and Max explore why bats hang upside down and discover that it’s a clever way to rest, stay out of reach of some predators, and get ready to fly. With a Halloween twist, they uncover how bats grip a branch while they sleep, perform an upside-down landing, and find food in the dark. It’s a fun, not-so-spooky look at the science behind one of Halloween’s most famous animals!

items.title: Ep41. Why do we trick-or-treat at Halloween?
items.desc: In this episode, Lily and Max take a playful trip through time to discover why we trick-or-treat at Halloween and why our buckets fill with sweets! 🎃🍬 From harvest celebrations and little soul cakes to costumes, doorstep jokes and lanterns carved from turnips, they explore how centuries of traditions helped shape Halloween today.

items.title: Ep40. How does concrete stick bricks together?
items.desc: In this episode, Lily and Max investigate the grey stuff that holds a brick wall together. Is it really concrete? And how can something soft and squishy turn into a strong bond?Join them for a playful trip inside a brick’s tiny pores to discover what mortar is made of, what happens when cement meets water, and why the way bricks are stacked matters too. You’ll never look at a brick wall quite the same way again!

items.title: Ep39. How does sleep restore our energy?
items.desc: In this episode, Lily and Max follow energy through a busy day and a good night’s sleep. Where does the energy from our food go when we run and play? And if sleeping uses energy too, why do we wake up feeling refreshed? Discover how our bodies turn food into movement and warmth, and how sleep helps our brains and bodies recover for tomorrow.
